summary: A monthly report of ARPANET traffic for October 1973. It tabulates, for each Host, how many packets it sent, split between traffic that stayed within its own node and traffic sent to other nodes, with daily averages. It is a data memo and defines no protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 586 publishes Host traffic statistics for October 1973. Its tables show packets sent within a node and between nodes, along with totals for the month.

subtitle: Host-by-host packet output statistics for the ARPANET in October 1973.

tldr.problem: The document provides a record of network traffic sent by each Host during October 1973.
tldr.mechanism: It lists packets output by Host, split into inter-node and intra-node counts, with totals and daily averages.
tldr.outcome: RFC 586 is a statistics report rather than a protocol specification, and the unit metadata says it updates RFC 579.

today: The unit records RFC 586's status as Unknown and says it updates RFC 579. It is a monthly Host traffic statistics report for October 1973.

sections.title: October Host Traffic Statistics
sections.content:
A. McKenzie attaches Host traffic statistics for October 1973. The attachment is titled “Host Throughput Summary (Packets Output)” and lists traffic for individual Hosts at network sites.

Where a site has multiple Hosts, the table lists separate Host rows and a combined site total. It also includes daily-average and day-count columns.
sections.plainLanguage: The report counts packets sent by individual Hosts during October 1973. Sites with more than one Host have separate rows and a subtotal.

sections.title: How to Read the Counts
sections.content:
The table separates inter-node packets from intra-node packets and gives a total. It also shows an average daily internode figure and the number of days counted for each Host or site subtotal.

Several rows explicitly say that a site had no traffic. The report is a collection of measured counts and does not explain the cause of differences between Hosts.
sections.plainLanguage: One column counts traffic between nodes, another counts traffic within a node, and a total combines the two. The report gives averages but does not explain why Hosts have different counts.

sections.title: Monthly Totals
sections.content:
The final lines report 93,524,810 internode packets and 23,672,870 intranode packets. The corresponding daily averages shown are 3,016,929 and 763,641.

The report also lists average counts per node-day and a packets/messages ratio for internode traffic. These are the report's statistics for the stated month.
sections.plainLanguage: The final rows add up packet counts across the listed Hosts. They also show average daily counts and a ratio for internode packets to messages.

references.text: RFC 579, the earlier traffic statistics report updated by this RFC.
